summary: Formatting/cleanup helper that builds a string in the output buffer a2 and strips the trailing file extension. When a1 or a2 is null it returns a1 unchanged. Otherwise it clears a2, invokes sub_568910(128), formats the local stack string v4 into a2 with the '%s' format string, then scans backward from the end of a2 for a '.' (46) byte and truncates the string there. Returns 0 on the success path.

Set result to 0 and compute v3 = &a2[strlen(a2)] as the pointer to the null terminator at the end of the formatted string in a2.
Scan backward from the string end while the byte at v3 is not '.' (46), decrementing v3 until it reaches a2 (start of the buffer) or finds a dot.
When a '.' byte is found, truncate the string there by writing the null terminator: *v3 = 0, removing the file extension.
Return result: 0 on the success path, or a1 unchanged when either argument is null.
